metaDescription: Free online MongoDB aggregation pipeline builder. Fill in match, unwind, lookup, group, sort, project, skip and limit stages for mongosh, Node or PyMongo.
intro: Build an aggregation pipeline from form fields: $match, $unwind, $lookup, $group, $sort, $project, $skip and $limit. Output as mongosh, Node.js driver, PyMongo or plain JSON.
why:
Aggregation pipelines are powerful but fiddly to type: nested braces, dollar signs on field references and a stage order that matters. A missing bracket costs time, and translating a working mongosh query into Python or Node adds another chance for error.

Fill in only the stages you need and the tool assembles them in a sensible order: match first, then unwind, lookup, group, sort, project, skip and limit. Accumulators are written as name:op:field, for example total:sum:amount. You pick the output language, and get a snippet ready to paste. It builds a basic pipeline, not every operator MongoDB offers, so extend the result by hand for expressions and conditions. Nothing leaves your browser.
howTo: Enter the collection name and choose the output format.
Fill in the stages you need, such as a $match JSON filter and a $group field.
Write accumulators as name:op:field, separated by commas.
Add sort, skip and limit, then copy the generated pipeline.

faq.q: Which stages and accumulators are supported?
faq.a: Stages: $match, $unwind, $lookup, $group, $sort, $project, $skip and $limit. Accumulators: sum, avg, min, max, first, last, push, addToSet and count. Others you add by hand.

faq.q: In what order are stages added?
faq.a: In a fixed order: match, unwind, lookup, group, sort, project, skip, limit. If you need a different order, copy the JSON output and rearrange the stages.

faq.q: How do I group all documents together?
faq.a: Enter null as the group field. The _id of the group becomes null, so accumulators run over the whole collection, which is useful for totals and averages.
No. It only generates code. Test the pipeline on a copy of your data or with explain before running it on production.
